content.title: About
content.content: Whopper with cheese is Burger King’s signature burger made with a flame‑grilled beef patty, melted cheese, fresh vegetables, sauce and a sesame‑seed bun. The grilling gives it a distinctive smoky flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original Whopper was introduced in 1957 in the United States.
The cheese version appeared in the early 2000s to meet growing demand for cheesier burgers.
It is sold in more than 100 countries worldwide.
Ingredients may vary slightly to meet regional regulations.
Burger King uses 100 % beef with no fillers.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Red meat is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The burger contains B12, B6 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Lettuce, tomato and onion contribute a modest amount of dietary fiber.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: A Whopper with cheese contains roughly 700–800 kcal, which can contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Saturated fat and sodium
items.content: The burger is relatively high in saturated fats and salt, which may affect cardiovascular health.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Contains milk, gluten, and soy (in the sauce), which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some components may include food additives that are unsuitable for people with sensitivities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burger is served in its classic bun and is meant to be eaten by hand. You can add extra sauce, remove the bun, or swap it for a whole‑grain version for a healthier twist.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burger in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage, reheat in an oven or microwave to restore the bun’s texture.
